newsitem.title: USA: Netters' favorite Web sites not always most popular.
newsitem.headline: Netters' favorite Web sites not always most popular.

text.p: The second "Cool Site of the Year" awards were handed out recently, and it was no surprise that well-heeled Web sites Discovery Channel, Salon and Hotwired were among the winners, based on superior design, deft execution, technical know-how and all around hipness.
But what professional Web-reviewers deem to be cool is one thing. What the Web masses consider cool enough to visit every day is another.
An informal poll of several dozen Internet regulars showed that people's favourite Web stomping grounds are as unique as the individuals who bookmark them.

Some netheads couldn't begin the day without checking in at CNN Interactive (http://www.cnn.com/), Yahoo News (http://www.yahoo.com/News/), WashingtonPost.com (http://www.washingtonpost.com/) or other sites that let them scan headlines, stocks or sports scores. Funnies fans frequent Dilbert (http://www.unitedmedia.com/comics/dilbert/), the hapless comic-strip geek-hero.

Others prefer Web sites such as Microsoft (http://www.microsoft.com/), The Ultimate Collection of Winsock Software (http://www.tucows.com/), MacInTouch (http://www.macintouch.com/) and Shareware.com (http://www.shareware.com/) to hone their computer skills and keep their hard drives loaded with shareware.
Still others use the Web as an electronic escape hatch, a digital fantasy land of games, chat rooms, TV fan clubs and music.
Some egoists prefer their own home pages to anything else -- could they be the same people who bore their friends with home videos?

Like a lot of Web-sters, Dave Burke likes to read the news online, but he doesn't like to hunt for it. His favourite Web sites are My Yahoo (http://www.my.yahoo.com) and Create Your Own Newspaper (http://crayon.net), which let readers create personalized news alerts with headlines, weather reports, sports scores and more from a variety of sources.

Some of Trent Glascock's favourite Web sites help him track investments. Among his top picks are Yahoo Quotes (http://quote.yahoo.com/), Smart Stock Mutual Funds (http://www.stocksmart.com/ss-doc/mutualfunds.html), which ranks the performance of 5,411 mutual funds, and Glassman on Wall Street (http://wp2.washingtonpost.com/wp-srv/business/glassman.htm), a digital version of James K. Glassman's Washington Post investment column, packaged with message boards and financial resources.

Kenji Kerins uses the Web as a traffic monitor. Kerins, a commercial photographer in Chicago, routinely tunes in Travel Times (http://www.ai.eecs.uic.edu/GCM/tt.html) for up-to-the-minute traffic reports for Chicago area expressway traffic.

"The data is gathered by sensors in the roads and transmitted to a computer where I can get the actual travel time between sensors at various parts in the expressway system," Kerins said. "It can make or break my day."

Greg Costikyan favours intellectual Web sites: the e-zine Salon (http://www.salon1999.com/); Thomas (http://thomas.loc.gov/), from the Library of Congress; The Tree of Life (http://phylogeny.arizona.edu/tree/phylogeny.html), a hyperlinked guide to species and classes of animal life on Earth, and The Game Cabinet (http://www.gamecabinet.com), with reviews of board games and discussions of game design issues. "Not for twitch-game players," Costikyan said.

Travers Naran just wants to be entertained. That's why one of his favourite Web sites is The Lurker's Guide to Babylon 5 (http://www.hyperion.com/lurk/), a fan-run site devoted to the syndicated sci-fi TV show.

For "yucks," Internet user Leslie Walker dials into The Daily Muse (http://www.cais.net/aschnedr//muse1.htm), Suck (http://www.suck.com/), and Stale (http://www.stale.com/), a tongue-in-cheek parody of Slate, Microsoft's high-brow e-zine.

Colin Scott McDonald set up his browser so the first thing he sees when he logs onto the Web is Over the Hedge (http://www.unitedmedia.com/comics/hedge), a comic tale of a racoon and turtle and their love affair with electronic gadgets.
But McDonald's real favourite is his own Web site, The Urban Dragon Home Page (http://www.flsig.org/people/scott), full of sketches of cartoon dragons with names like Draco Shius Maximus.

Fred Holborn is a fan of his own work too. Holborn, who runs an Irvine, Calif., intranet design and installation business, doesn't believe in all work and no play. That's why he built an interactive compass into his company's Web site (http://www.onlinecp.com/).
"Click on the compass points for views from around the world and from the Space Shuttle when flying," Holborn said.
Guess it beats home videos.
The following won InfiNet's "Cool Site of the Year" (http://cool.infi.net/csoty.html) honours for 1996. (Judges selected five nominees in each category, and winners were voted on by the public):
- Site, and design: Discovery Channel (http://www.discovery.com/)
- Still cool (past winner that's still hot): Hotwired (http://www.hotwired.com/)
- Personal home page: Timothy Leary Home Page (http://www.leary.com:8081/)
- Designers: Mignon Khargie and Elizabeth Kairys for Salon (http://www.salon1999.com/)
- Innovation: Java (http://java.sun.com)
- Site script: Ask Dr. Science (http://www.ducksbreath.com/)
- Directory: Alta Vista (http://www.altavista.digital.com)
- Browser: Netscape Navigator (http://www.netscape.com)
(Michelle V. Rafter writes about cyberspace and technology from Los Angeles. Reach her at mvrafter(at)deltanet.com. Opinions expressed in this column are hers alone).
